about.title: Corte Madera Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Corte Madera is a small town, but its shopping destinations along Tamalpais Drive and Paradise Drive draw steady foot traffic from across Marin County, and that traffic means spills, uneven walkways, and poorly lit stairwells happen. When a property owner fails to notice or fix a hazard, California law may hold them responsible, but only if you can show they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the danger. That's why documenting the scene matters so much here: photos of the spill or broken tile, the names of any employees or witnesses nearby, and a request to preserve store surveillance footage before it gets overwritten. LawProactive isn't a law firm, but we connect people injured in falls with an independent attorney who can help gather that evidence and evaluate what happened. There's no cost to get connected, and any attorney in our network works on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Timing Matter in Corte Madera

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability requires showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to act. An attorney can help pull maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to build that notice argument.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many stores and complexes near Tamalpais Drive and Paradise Drive overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Sending a preservation request quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Your Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim, and far less time if a government entity owns the property. Pure comparative fault also means your own recovery isn't automatically wiped out even if you were partly careless, but the clock doesn't wait.

items.question: I fell at a Corte Madera store but didn't report it right away. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: You can still pursue a claim, though reporting promptly and documenting conditions helps preserve evidence. An independent attorney can look at what records still exist, including surveillance footage, incident reports, or witness accounts, and advise on next steps.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the fall, like not watching where I was walking?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't necessarily bar you from recovering. Your compensation may simply be reduced by your share of fault, which an attorney can help assess based on the specific facts.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a slip and fall claim in Corte Madera?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the injury under California law. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a town facility, the deadline is much shorter, so it's worth getting guidance early.
